look_here_first: FIRST photograph stem BASE: Engelmann’s sage has cauline (stem) leaves but no persistent basal-leaf set. Narrow linear leaf blades ~30–60 × 3–5 mm. THEN count flowers in axillary cymes (three per cyme) and examine the ten-ribbed 10–11 mm calyx with short awned tips. Tack-shaped subsessile glands require true macro; never pretend broad shot proves them.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial low dense clump with many stems.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Only cauline narrow leaves; paired bases can form a short sheath across the node.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: 3-flowered cymes repeated at closely spaced nodes.

key_traits.label: Calyx
key_traits.text: Strongly 10-ridged with short awned lobe tips.

key_traits.label: Floral detail
key_traits.text: Pale blue-violet corolla with a broad white/violet-marked lower lip.

key_traits.label: Leaf measurement
key_traits.text: Cauline linear leaves typically ~30–60 mm long and 3–5 mm wide (UT Austin Williamson County morphology).

key_traits.label: Calyx measurement
key_traits.text: Calyx ~10–11 mm long, 10-ridged with short ~0.5 mm awns and tack-shaped glands (microscope/strong macro needed).

key_traits.label: Flower group
key_traits.text: Two opposite axillary cymes at each flowering node, typically 3 flowers per cyme.

key_traits.label: Corolla
key_traits.text: Blue-violet with conspicuous white/violet-marked lower lip; corolla approximately 18–22 mm (UT Austin); can overlap Texas sage.
